The strategic tension centers on whether Flutter's depressed starting Owner Earnings ($1.61/share normalized) represent transient sporting outcome variance and integration friction, or a permanent impairment of platform unit economics. Skeptics highlight reported Average Monthly Player (AMP) contraction—slipping 11% YoY to 14.29 million—alongside regulatory cancellations abroad, headlined by India's abrupt ban on real-money gaming that wiped out Junglee Games and triggered a $556M impairment. Consequently, the market prices in a promotional 'generosity trap' where U.S. market leadership can only be protected via elevated reinvestment that permanently curbs free cash flow conversion.
